records.title: Bitquery Research — Who Actually Uses the XRP Ledger? 5.06B transaction adoption audit
records.note: Bitquery reports counting XRPL transactions from 2013-01 through 2026-09-08. Its August 2026 analysis attributes 93.2% of traffic to 793 accounts, with 767 classified as machines; its 'human-scale' filter leaves 0.80% of traffic. It reports 2.645M x402-memo payments from 142 accounts, 59,541 DEX accounts, 58 payment-channel accounts, 76 MPT/tokenized-asset accounts and 15 permissioned-domain accounts over the 12 months to August. It reports genuine RLUSD issuer rMxCKbEDwqr76QuheSUMdEGf4B9xJ8m5De, USD1.024B outstanding, top 10 addresses holding 81.6%, top 100 holding 99%, and about 1,000–2,500 wallets receiving normal transfers in a typical month. It reports no bank/payment-company names in declared XRPL domains. Methodology counts senders, uses delivered values rather than declared partial-payment amounts, filters RLUSD by issuer address and measures all account balances. Ownership labels and 'human-scale' classifications are behavioral inferences; the audit covers public XRPL on-ledger activity and cannot observe CEX internal books, private/off-ledger rails, OTC or all institutional custody.

records.title: DailyCoin — XRP's $43 Billion Jump Came On a $44 Million Flow; Zach Rector's 986x claim
records.note: DailyCoin reports Zach Rector's use of CoinGlass four-hour exchange-flow data for 2026-08-19 through 2026-08-21: approximately USD105M exchange inflows and USD60M outflows, net USD44.3M, while XRP market capitalization allegedly rose USD43.74B. The article reports a 986x market-cap-change/netflow ratio (other coverage cites 987x depending on precision). This is a ratio between market-cap valuation change and exchange-wallet net transfers, not a measure of new fiat capital or a causal capital multiplier. Exchange transfers do not equal executed purchases and omit/underrepresent OTC, internal transfers, collateral movements, derivatives, market makers and other venues.

records.title: Vling channel directory — Kamilah Stevenson, candidate YouTube channel UCqUPJMQdkCN6lsLVDnichPA
records.note: Vling associates channel ID UCqUPJMQdkCN6lsLVDnichPA and handle @drkamilahstevenson with Kamilah Stevenson; it reports approximately 143K subscribers and 1.2K videos. Another directory, CryptoKrios, reports 103K subscribers and 633 videos analyzed, which is an analysis sample rather than a verified total inventory. Direct YouTube channel-page retrieval was too large/throttled in this research pass. Public video transcripts self-introduce as 'Camila Stevenson'; an interview host addresses the creator as 'Camilla'. This is a plausible candidate for the user's 'Camilla Stephenson' reference, but spelling/identity equivalence is not proven. Do not claim this is the exact person without corroboration.
